nodes.label: API client
nodes.summary: Sends requests identified by an API key, user or IP.

nodes.label: API gateway / proxy
nodes.summary: Interceptor on the request path. Applies the limiter before any backend work happens.
nodes.details: Envoy runs the limiter as an HTTP filter in front of the services `[CONFIRMED]`.

nodes.label: Local token bucket
nodes.summary: Per-node in-memory bucket. No network call. Absorbs large bursts so the global service is not overwhelmed.
nodes.details: Envoy: a local token bucket "can absorb very large bursts in load that might otherwise overwhelm a global rate limit service". The recommended shape is local first, then global.

nodes.label: Global rate-limit service
nodes.summary: Called over gRPC for each request on routes that enable it. Returns allow or over-limit for a descriptor.
nodes.details: If the call fails: `failure_mode_deny=true` returns 500, otherwise the request is allowed through (counted as `failure_mode_allowed`). The page does not state the default.

nodes.label: Counter store (Redis / memcached)
nodes.summary: Shared fast counters. The check-and-update must be atomic: INCR with EXPIRE in a Lua script or MULTI/EXEC.
nodes.details: Stripe uses Redis. Cloudflare uses Twemproxy + Twemcache with GET/SET/atomic INCR and avoids compare-and-swap because of contention during attacks. Redis documents the INCR/EXPIRE race and its fixes.

nodes.label: Load shedders
nodes.summary: Stripe's fleet-usage and worker-utilisation shedders: reject non-critical traffic (503) when the fleet is busy, test-mode first.
nodes.details: Fleet usage shedder reserves capacity for critical methods using a Redis cluster counting requests of each type. The worker shedder is the "final line of defense" during incidents.

nodes.label: Limits config + kill switch
nodes.summary: Per-key, per-route limits, hot-reloaded. Feature flags let operators disable a limiter that misfires.
nodes.details: Stripe: dark-launch each limiter to see what it would block, and keep kill switches and alerting.

nodes.label: Upstream API
nodes.summary: The protected backend. Only sees traffic that passed the limiter.

steps.caption: The request arrives with an API key.
First stage: a local token bucket takes a token with no network call. It absorbs bursts cheaply.
Second stage: the gateway asks the global rate-limit service about this key's descriptor.
The service updates the shared counter with one atomic operation. Read-then-write would race.
Load shedders check fleet health and drop non-critical traffic only when the fleet is saturated.
Within limits: the request reaches the backend.
A client that has used its allowance sends another request.
The global service reports the descriptor is over limit.
The gateway answers 429 and a back-off hint (Retry-After; the IETF RateLimit headers are still a draft).
The global check fails because its store is unreachable.

Failing open: errors are caught so the API stays up (Stripe), or Envoy lets the request through when failure_mode_deny is false. Abuse gets through until the store recovers, so alert and keep a kill switch.
